sn22.49:4.7: This directly rejects all forms of self, but especially the Upaniṣadic view, which the Pali directly echoes. _Eso’hamasmi_ is identical with Yājñavalkya’s _so’hamasmīti_ (“I am that”, Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.4.1), while Uddālaka’s _tattvamasi_ is the same phrase in second person (“you are that”, Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.7). The same passage also parallels _eso me attā_ with _sa ātmā_ (“that is the self”).  See too Uddālaka’s, “I am that, I indeed am that” (_iyam aham asmīyam aham asmīti_, Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.10.1; cf. 4.11.1, 4.12.1, 8.11.1–2). Yājñavalkya further says, “I myself am that person” (_yo’sāvasau puruṣaḥ so’hamasmi_, Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 5.15 = Īśā Upaniṣad 16). Depending on context, similar phrases might also depict the one who is attached to a false, limited self, thinking “I am he”, “this is mine” (_ahaṁ so, mamedaṁ_, Maitrī Upaniṣad 3.2).
